title: Photo-Fenton assisted degradation of methylene blue dye utilizing green tea extract synthesized Ag@Fe 2 O 3  nanocomposites
content: The discharge of synthetic dyes into water resources represents a significant and persistent environmental concern, making their removal from aquatic systems essential. The use of iron-based nanomaterials has emerged as a promising approach for the degradation of synthetic dyes in contaminated water. Herein, we report an environmentally friendly method for the synthesis of Ag@Fe2O3 nanocomposites (Ag@Fe2O3 NCs) utilizing green tea extract as a reducing agent for the photo-Fenton-assisted degradation of methylene blue (MB) dye under visible-light irradiation. X-ray diffraction (XRD), UV-visible diffuse reflectance spectroscopy (DRS), photoluminescence spectroscopy (PL), field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), field-emission transmission electron microscopy (FETEM), and Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) analysis were employed to characterize the synthesized materials. The XRD pattern confirmed the formation of a rhombohedral structure with Fe2O3 and exhibited peaks corresponding to the cubic phase of Ag. UV-vis DRS results indicated that the electronic transitions in the spectra are due to ligand-to-metal charge transfer and a double-exciton process, and the initial bandgap energy of Fe2O3 nanoparticles (Fe2O3 NPs) decreased upon incorporation of Ag. FESEM analysis displayed a spherical morphology with some pore formation within the Ag@Fe2O3 nanostructure, offering exposure to binding sites for MB adsorption. The synthesized Ag@Fe2O3 nanocatalyst showed a remarkable photo-Fenton degradation efficiency of 91.97% in the presence of H2O2, attributed to the generation of ˙OH and ˙O2− radicals, with oxidative holes (h+) confirmed to be the major contributors. Ag acts as an electron sink and imparts high-energy electrons induced by localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) effects. Moreover, kinetic studies showed that the photocatalytic degradation of MB followed the pseudo-first-order kinetic model, while the adsorption degradation followed pseudo-second-order kinetics. Furthermore, a possible photo-Fenton synergistic mechanism is proposed. This study presents novel and deep insights into the design of photo-Fenton degradation systems using Ag coupled with a Fe2O3 semiconductor. These findings offer valuable insights into the potential of green-synthesized nanomaterials for enhanced environmental remediation applications.
